TITLE: Escape aimed at the Aa popover, Directions dialog or Find Text input closes the whole question modal
FILE: src/components/drill/shared/LRQuestionModal.tsx:136
SEVERITY CLAIMED: major
SCENARIO: In the capstone modal, pick an answer, cross out two choices, add a highlight, then open the 'Aa' text-size popover and press Escape to dismiss it. Radix closes the popover via a document capture-phase keydown listener that calls preventDefault but not stopPropagation; the event continues to window where the modal's own listener calls props.onClose(). The modal unmounts and all local state (selected, eliminated, highlights) is lost. Same for Escape pressed inside the new Find Text input. This path did not exist before the toolbar was added to the modal.
EVIDENCE: React.useEffect(() => {
  const onKey = (e: KeyboardEvent) => { if (e.key === "Escape") props.onClose(); };
  window.addEventListener("keydown", onKey);
  ...
}, [props.onClose]);
// @radix-ui/react-use-escape-keydown: ownerDocument.addEventListener("keydown", handleKeyDown, { capture: true }) - no stopPropagation
PROPOSED FIX: In the modal's Escape handler ignore events that were already handled (if (e.defaultPrevented) return;) and ignore Escape when the target is inside a Radix layer or a text input ((e.target as HTMLElement).closest('[data-radix-popper-content-wrapper], [role=dialog], input')). Better: gate onClose on there being no open popover/dialog (lift aaOpen/directionsOpen state or use the defaultPrevented check, which Radix sets).

import * as React from "react";

const Popover = PopoverPrimitive.Root;

const PopoverTrigger = PopoverPrimitive.Trigger;

const PopoverContent = React.forwardRef<
  React.ElementRef<typeof PopoverPrimitive.Content>,
  React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<typeof PopoverPrimitive.Content>
>(({ className, align = "center", sideOffset = 4, ...props }, ref) => (
  <PopoverPrimitive.Portal>
    <PopoverPrimitive.Content
      ref={ref}
      align={align}
      sideOffset={sideOffset}
      className={cn(
        "z-[1000] w-72 rounded-md border bg-popover p-4 text-popover-foreground shadow-md outline-none data-[state=open]:animate-in data-[state=closed]:animate-out data-[state=closed]:fade-out-0 data-[state=open]:fade-in-0 data-[state=closed]:zoom-out-95 data-[state=open]:zoom-in-95 data-[side=bottom]:slide-in-from-top-2 data-[side=left]:slide-in-from-right-2 data-[side=right]:slide-in-from-left-2 data-[side=top]:slide-in-from-bottom-2",
        className,
      )}
      {...props}

));
PopoverContent.displayName = PopoverPrimitive.Content.displayName;

export { Popover, PopoverTrigger, PopoverContent };

import { defineConfig } from "vitest/config";
import react from "@vitejs/plugin-react-swc";
import path from "path";

// Force test mode for Vitest even if the shell exports NODE_ENV=production.
// Without this, Vite pre-bundles React in production mode and react/jsx-dev-runtime
// drops jsxDEV, breaking every component test with "jsxDEV is not a function".
// Must run before the react() plugin and dep optimization read NODE_ENV.
process.env.NODE_ENV = "test";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react()],
  test: {
    environment: "jsdom",
    globals: true,
    setupFiles: ["./src/test/setup.ts"],
    include: ["src/**/*.{test,spec}.{ts,tsx}"],
    exclude: ["e2e/**", "node_modules/**", "dist/**"],
    // Multi-step interaction tests (drill labs) chain many fireEvent + waitFor
    // cycles. Under the full parallel run the default 5s is too tight and they
    // time out despite passing in isolation. Give heavy component tests headroom.
    testTimeout: 15000,
  },
  resolve: {
    alias: { "@": path.resolve(__dirname, "./src") },
  },
});
